title: REPORT on the European Semester for economic policy coordination: employment and social priorities for 2025
part_text: 37. Regrets the ever-increasing role of the unelected Commission in the fiscal affairs of the Member States through mechanisms such as the European Semester and revised fiscal rules; believes this centralisation undermines national democracies and damages the ability of people to put trust in political systems to solve their problems; notes that the Commission has engaged in significant overreach through the European Semester process when it comes to public policy areas that legally fall under the competence of the Member States under the TFEU, such as pensions and the provision of healthcare; regrets that the revised economic governance framework fails to enhance social progress and convergence and to foster the ecological transition; regrets further that in order to comply with the revised economic governance rules, governments of Member States have committed in their national fiscal and budgetary plans to reduce public expenditure and to implement structural reforms; deplores that these commitments have already or will in the near future translate into concrete measures deeply affecting the population, such as the reform of the pension system, the reform of the unemployment scheme, lower healthcare reimbursements, and job cuts in public administrations such as public education, leading to the general degradation of public services; warns that these economic policies, aimed at complying with the objectives of the European Semester, will have harmful and long-lasting impacts on the people and on our collective capacity to cope with the ecological crisis, while at the same time failing to achieve the deficit and debt reduction for which they are intended; reiterates that instead of focusing on irrelevant economic indicators and pursuing endless debt and deficit reduction, the EU economic governance should aim at eradicating poverty and inequalities, provide a high level of social protection, high-quality public services, and individual and collective well-being through the fulfilment of the essential needs of all citizens and ecological planning; notes that the involvement of social partners and civil society should be enhanced in the economic governance and the European Semester; insists that the Commission should reinforce its dialogues with the Member States on the implementation of existing recommendations and of the employment guidelines, as well as on current or future policy action to address identified challenges;
